title: Mock 5 · Advisory Practice
blurb: Risk profiling, NPS/UPS/PPF details, grandfathering and practical adviser judgement, with a short client-behaviour caselet.

questions.q: Anil credits his five-fold gain to his own skill and wants to raise his equity exposure sharply. Which bias does this reflect?
questions.explanation: Overconfident investors overestimate their judgement and confuse luck with skill. Self-attribution intensifies it. The workbook warns that one winning bet may tempt a client to over-invest and modify the asset allocation.
hints: Incorrect. Loss aversion would make him avoid risk, not seek it.
Incorrect. Mental accounting is treating money differently by source.
Correct. Treating luck as skill is overconfidence.
Incorrect. Status quo bias is preferring no change.
questions.case: Anil, 58, is a salaried manager who will retire in 2 years. His wife is a homemaker and fully dependent on him. His home loan is repaid and his retirement goal is already almost fully funded. Last year a small bet on a small-cap stock rose five-fold, and he now calls himself an 'aggressive' investor and wants 90% of his portfolio in small-cap funds. During the 2020 market crash, however, he sold all his equity funds within a week. His SEBI-registered investment adviser is preparing his risk profile.

questions.q: Compared with a 35-year-old who states the same risk tolerance, Anil's risk capacity is:
options: Lower, because he has less time before the funds are needed and has a dependent spouse
Higher, because he has more experience
The same, because their stated tolerance is the same
questions.explanation: Risk capacity depends on financial and temporal factors. The workbook gives the example that a 35-year-old 30 years from retirement has materially higher capacity than someone close to retirement, even with the same stated tolerance.
hints: Correct. A short horizon and a dependant mean lower capacity.
Incorrect. Experience does not increase capacity.
Incorrect. Capacity is objective and differs from tolerance.
Incorrect. Capacity must be assessed along with willingness.
questions.case: Anil, 58, is a salaried manager who will retire in 2 years. His wife is a homemaker and fully dependent on him. His home loan is repaid and his retirement goal is already almost fully funded. Last year a small bet on a small-cap stock rose five-fold, and he now calls himself an 'aggressive' investor and wants 90% of his portfolio in small-cap funds. During the 2020 market crash, however, he sold all his equity funds within a week. His SEBI-registered investment adviser is preparing his risk profile.

questions.q: What should the adviser do, given Anil's profile?
options: Implement 90% small-cap as the client has asked
Refuse to advise him at all
Base the risk profile only on his recent transaction history
Recommend a less aggressive allocation consistent with his capacity, composure and low risk need, and communicate the assessed profile and get his consent before advising
questions.explanation: Regulation 16 requires an objective assessment of willingness and ability to bear losses, communicated with consent before advice. High stated tolerance with low composure and a low risk need calls for a less aggressive allocation. Transaction history can only supplement the profile.
hints: Incorrect. Following an overconfident instruction ignores capacity and composure.
Incorrect. The adviser's role is to guide, not to walk away.
Incorrect. Transaction history cannot substitute for objective risk profiling.
Correct. Use an objective, consented profile and a moderated allocation.

His home loan is repaid and his retirement goal is already almost fully funded. Last year a small bet on a small-cap stock rose five-fold, and he now calls himself an 'aggressive' investor and wants 90% of his portfolio in small-cap funds. During the 2020 market crash, however, he sold all his equity funds within a week. His SEBI-registered investment adviser is preparing his risk profile.

questions.q: IRDAI requires insurers to provide ULIP benefit illustrations at which two assumed rates of return?
questions.explanation: ULIP regulations require benefit illustrations at 4% and 8%. The prospect signs the illustration with the proposal form, and the agent signs it too.
hints: Correct. The two rates are 4% and 8%.
Incorrect. 6% and 10% are not the IRDAI-prescribed illustration rates.
Incorrect. 5% and 9% are not the IRDAI-prescribed illustration rates.
Incorrect. 8% and 12% would overstate returns; the prescribed pair is 4% and 8%.

questions.q: To work out the return earned on the extra premium paid for a 'return of premium' term plan over a pure term plan, which Excel function does the workbook use?
questions.explanation: The workbook computes the inherent return with RATE: Nper = term, PMT = extra premium, PV = 0, FV = premiums returned, type = 1. In its example this gives 4.88%.
hints: Correct. RATE solves for the return.
Incorrect. PMT solves for the periodic payment.
Incorrect. NPER solves for the number of periods.
Incorrect. PV solves for present value.

questions.q: A person needs term cover of ₹8 crore. The insurer's telescopic premium rates stop falling beyond ₹2 crore. What does the workbook suggest?
options: Buy one ₹8 crore policy from one insurer
Buy ₹8 crore from eight different insurers
Buy only ₹2 crore since the rest is not cost-efficient
Buy four policies of ₹2 crore each from the same insurer, so some can be dropped as needs fall
questions.explanation: Because telescopic benefits stop at a certain level, buying, for example, 4 policies of ₹2 crore each from the same company keeps the low rate and gives the option to give up some policies later as insurance needs fall.
hints: Incorrect. A single policy cannot be partially dropped later.
Incorrect. Many insurers add complexity, and the telescopic benefit is per insurer.
Incorrect. This leaves the family under-insured.
Correct. Multiple ₹2 crore policies give flexibility at the same rate.

questions.q: Which of the following will a liability insurance policy (e.g. professional indemnity) NOT cover?
options: Damages arising from the insured's intentional or criminal acts
Legal costs of defending a suit by a third party
Damages payable for negligence to a client
Compensation for third-party property damage for which the insured is liable
questions.explanation: Liability insurance indemnifies damages payable under law to third parties and defence costs, but will not cover intentional damage or damages caused by criminal activities.
hints: Correct. Intentional and criminal acts are excluded.
Incorrect. Defence costs are covered.
Incorrect. Negligence-based liability is covered.
Incorrect. Third-party property damage liability is covered.

questions.q: Why is an employer not allowed simply to pay pensions to retired employees out of its current revenue?
options: Because the Income-tax Act prohibits employers from paying any pension
AS-15 requires retirement benefits to be provided in the year of accrual, and annuities from such funds are life insurance business that must go through an IRDAI-registered insurer
Because SEBI regulates all pension payments
Because pensions can only be paid through the EPFO
questions.explanation: Paying from current revenue depends on the employer's financial health. AS-15 requires provisioning on accrual, and s.2(11) of the Insurance Act treats superannuation annuities as life insurance business, so payments go through an IRDAI-registered life insurer (with funding via insurer or trust).
hints: Incorrect. The IT Act regulates tax treatment, not a ban on pensions.
Correct. Accrual accounting plus Insurance Act requirements.
Incorrect. SEBI does not regulate superannuation pensions.
Incorrect. Superannuation is separate from EPFO schemes.

questions.q: A PPF account was opened on 10 August 2020. From which financial year can the first partial withdrawal be made?
questions.explanation: Partial withdrawal is allowed after completion of 5 financial years from the end of the FY in which the account was opened. The FY of opening is 2020-21, so withdrawals are allowed from FY 2025-26 (mirroring the workbook's Feb 2017 to FY 2021-22 example).
hints: Incorrect. FY 2023-24 falls in the loan window (FY 3–6), not the withdrawal window.
Incorrect. This adds one year too many.
Incorrect. This is the year after maturity, not the first withdrawal year.
Correct. FY of opening 2020-21 plus 5 gives FY 2025-26.

questions.q: What is the minimum annual contribution under NPS Vatsalya?
questions.explanation: NPS Vatsalya requires a minimum contribution of ₹250 a year with no maximum. A separate PRAN is allotted in the child's name.
hints: Incorrect. ₹500 is the minimum per NPS Tier I contribution.
Correct. The minimum is ₹250 a year.
Incorrect. ₹1,000 is the NPS Tier I minimum yearly contribution.
Incorrect. A minimum of ₹250 applies.

questions.q: Under the Unified Pension Scheme, what is the assured payout after a minimum of 25 years of qualifying service?
options: 50% of the average basic pay of the 12 months immediately before superannuation
50% of the last drawn basic pay plus DA
60% of the average basic pay of the last 10 months
questions.explanation: UPS assures 50% of the 12-month average basic pay before superannuation after 25 years' service (proportionate for 10–25 years), with a minimum of ₹10,000 per month after 10 years. The family payout is 60%.
hints: Correct. 50% of the 12-month average basic.
Incorrect. It is the 12-month average basic, not the last basic plus DA.
Incorrect. 60% is the family payout. The averaging period is 12 months.
Incorrect. ₹10,000 is only the minimum guaranteed payout.

questions.q: A client needs ₹9,00,000 in the first year of a 30-year retirement and will hold 30% in equity. Using the workbook's SWR table (3.70% for 30% equity over 30 years), what corpus is required?
questions.explanation: Corpus = annual income ÷ SWR = 9,00,000 ÷ 0.037 = ₹2,43,24,324, about ₹2.43 crore.
hints: Incorrect. This multiplies by the SWR instead of dividing.
Incorrect. This would correspond to an SWR of about 3.33%.
Correct. ₹9 lakh ÷ 3.70% ≈ ₹2.43 crore.
Incorrect. ₹1.62 crore corresponds to a ₹6 lakh need.

questions.q: Mr. K, an Indian citizen, has Indian income of ₹20 lakh, spends only 50 days in India, and is not liable to tax in any other country because of his domicile or residence. His status for the tax year is:
options: Non-resident, since he stayed less than 60 days
Deemed resident, treated as Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident
Not taxable in India at all
questions.explanation: An Indian citizen whose Indian income exceeds ₹15 lakh and who is not taxable in any other country is deemed resident regardless of stay, and is always treated as RNOR.
hints: Incorrect. The deemed-residence rule overrides the day count.
Incorrect. A deemed resident is always NOR.
Correct. Deemed resident means RNOR.
Incorrect. His Indian income is taxable.

questions.q: Shares bought on 1 June 2016 at ₹150 had a fair market value of ₹240 on 31 January 2018. They are sold on the exchange (STT paid) in 2026 at ₹200. What is the long-term capital gain per share?
questions.explanation: Grandfathered cost = higher of actual cost (₹150) and the lower of FMV on 31-1-2018 (₹240) and the sale price (₹200), which is ₹200. LTCG = 200 − 200 = 0. Grandfathering cannot create a loss.
hints: Incorrect. This ignores grandfathering and uses the actual cost.
Correct. Cost = max(150, min(240, 200)) = 200, so the gain is nil.
Incorrect. Grandfathering cannot turn a gain into a loss.
Incorrect. This mixes up FMV and cost.

questions.q: Mr. X follows the mercantile system of accounting. How is interest on his listed bonds taxed?
options: On an accrual basis, under Income from Other Sources
questions.explanation: Under s.276 (old s.145), interest on securities is computed per the regularly employed method of accounting: accrual under the mercantile system and receipt under the cash system. It falls under Other Sources unless it is business income.
hints: Incorrect. Receipt basis applies to the cash system.
Incorrect. Interest is not a capital gain.
Correct. Mercantile means accrual.
Incorrect. Interest is taxed at applicable rates.

questions.q: To claim the beneficial DTAA rate, a non-resident must furnish a Tax Residency Certificate and which form under the Income-tax Rules, 2026?
questions.explanation: To claim DTAA relief, the non-resident needs a TRC from the country of residence and must furnish Form 41 (earlier Form 10F), a self-declaration with prescribed details.
hints: Incorrect. Form 16 is the salary TDS certificate.
Correct. TRC plus Form 41.
Incorrect. Form 15G is a no-TDS declaration by residents, not a DTAA form.
Incorrect. 26AS is a tax credit statement.

questions.q: How is income from trading in equity futures and options on a recognised stock exchange through a registered broker treated?
options: As non-speculative business income, even though there is no delivery
questions.explanation: Derivative transactions on a recognised exchange are specifically excluded from 'speculative transaction' under s.66(31) (old 43(5)), so F&O income or loss is normal business income.
hints: Incorrect. The derivatives exclusion makes it non-speculative.
Incorrect. F&O traders' income is business income, not s.196 gains.
Incorrect. It is taxable.
Correct. F&O is non-speculative business.

questions.q: Mr. X took an endowment policy in June 2024 with a sum assured of ₹75 lakh and an annual premium of ₹6 lakh. How will the maturity proceeds be taxed?
options: Fully exempt, since the premium is within 10% of the sum assured
Taxable as Income from Other Sources, because the premium exceeds ₹5 lakh
Exempt only if he dies before maturity
questions.explanation: For non-ULIP policies issued on or after 1 April 2023, if premiums exceed ₹5 lakh the maturity proceeds are taxable as Income from Other Sources (net of premiums not claimed as deduction), even if the 10% condition is met.
hints: Incorrect. The ₹5 lakh aggregate premium cap overrides the 10% test.
Correct. Above ₹5 lakh premium means it is taxable as Other Sources.
Incorrect. Capital-gains treatment applies to high-premium ULIPs, not endowments.
Incorrect. Death proceeds are exempt anyway. The question is about maturity.

questions.q: Under Muslim personal law, a Muslim's bequest by Will (Wasiyat) generally cannot exceed what portion of the net estate without the heirs' consent?
questions.explanation: A Wasiyat generally cannot exceed one-third of the net estate (after funeral expenses and debts) without the heirs' consent, and it can even be oral.
hints: Incorrect. One-half is not the limit.
Incorrect. One-fourth is a widow's share in some cases.
Correct. The limit is one-third.
Incorrect. The whole estate cannot be bequeathed without consent.

questions.q: What is the key feature of joint tenancy compared with tenancy-in-common?
options: Each co-owner's share passes under his Will
No co-owner can possess the whole property
A right of survivorship, so a deceased joint tenant's interest passes to the surviving joint tenants
questions.explanation: In a valid joint tenancy, the deceased's interest passes by survivorship. Tenants-in-common hold undivided shares (equal if not stated) that devolve under the Will or succession law, with no survivorship.
hints: Incorrect. Passing under the Will describes tenancy-in-common.
Incorrect. Shares can be equal and are deemed equal if not stated.
Incorrect. Co-owners have rights to possess the whole property.
Correct. Survivorship is the defining feature of joint tenancy.

questions.q: Following the Repealing and Amending Act, 2025, what is the position on probate of a Will executed in Mumbai?
options: Probate remains compulsory for all Wills made in Mumbai, Chennai or Kolkata
Probate is now compulsory for all Wills across India
Probate is no longer mandatory merely because the Will was made within the former presidency towns
questions.explanation: Section 213 of the Indian Succession Act, which created compulsory probate for the former presidency towns, was omitted by the Repealing and Amending Act, 2025. Probate remains available to executors and where Wills are disputed.
hints: Incorrect. This was the old rule.
Incorrect. No such all-India mandate exists.
Correct. s.213 was omitted, so probate is no longer compulsory there.
Incorrect. Probate still exists and is available to executors.

questions.q: Which of the following is a premise of Prospect Theory?
options: People evaluate outcomes in absolute terms without any reference point
Gains hurt more than equivalent losses
People are risk-averse about gains but risk-seeking about losses
questions.explanation: Prospect theory (Kahneman and Tversky, 1979): choices are evaluated relative to a reference point, people are risk-averse in gains and risk-seeking in losses, and losses hurt more than gains.
hints: Incorrect. Outcomes are judged relative to a reference point.
Incorrect. Losses hurt more, not gains.
Incorrect. That is a standard finance assumption.
Correct. Risk-averse in gains and risk-seeking in losses.

questions.q: According to the workbook, which of the following works as an in-built 'nudge' that helps clients book profits high and buy low?
options: Frequent review of daily market news with the client
Pre-agreed ground rules on when to rebalance the asset allocation
Allowing the client to trade whenever he feels confident
Following last year's best-performing asset class
questions.explanation: Laying down advance ground rules, such as rebalancing triggers, that the client buys into creates built-in nudges: booking profits when an asset rises and buying when it falls.
hints: Incorrect. This encourages action bias.
Correct. Rebalancing rules are the nudge.
Incorrect. This feeds overconfidence and over-trading.
Incorrect. This is chasing performance.

questions.q: As per the workbook comparison, an ELSS fund must invest at least what share of its assets in equity and equity-related instruments, and what is its lock-in?
questions.explanation: ELSS is a diversified equity scheme required to invest at least 80% in equity and equity-related instruments, with a 3-year lock-in (the shortest among tax-saving instruments).
hints: Correct. 80% equity and 3 years.
Incorrect. 65% is the 'equity-oriented fund' tax definition, not the ELSS mandate.
Incorrect. The lock-in is 3 years, not 5 (5 years applies to tax-saving FDs).
Incorrect. These are not ELSS parameters.

questions.q: In Excel's PV function, entering 1 as the 'type' argument means:
options: Payments are made at the beginning of each period
Payments are made at the end of each period
questions.explanation: In PV and PMT, type 0 (or omitted) means payments at the period end and type 1 means payments at the beginning. The workbook uses 1 when the expenses are needed at the start of each year.
hints: Correct. Type 1 means the beginning of the period.
Incorrect. That is type 0 or omitted.
Incorrect. The rate convention is not set by 'type'.
Incorrect. FV is a separate argument.
